# throwaway

> Disposable & invalid email detector - bloom filter API on Cloudflare Workers

## What it does

Given an email address or domain, returns whether the TLD is a real ICANN-recognized suffix, whether the domain has MX records (can receive mail), whether Cloudflare family DNS appears to block the domain, and whether the domain is a known disposable/temporary email provider (mailinator, guerrillamail, etc). Uses the [disposable/disposable](https://github.com/disposable/disposable) list (72K+ domains) compiled into a bloom filter for fast O(1) lookups.

Use this before sending signup emails, creating accounts, or accepting form submissions to block throwaway addresses, non-existent domains, and syntactically invalid domains.

## API

Base URL: `https://throwaway.sslboard.com`

### Check a single email

```
GET /check?email=user@example.com
```

```json
{
  "email": "user@mailinator.com",
  "domain": "mailinator.com",
  "valid_tld": true,
  "has_mx": true,
  "dns_blocked": false,
  "disposable": true,
  "should_reject": true
}
```

### Check a single domain

```
GET /check?domain=example.com
```

```json
{
  "domain": "example.com",
  "valid_tld": true,
  "has_mx": true,
  "dns_blocked": false,
  "disposable": false,
  "should_reject": false
}
```

### Batch check emails

```
POST /check
Content-Type: application/json

{ "emails": ["a@mailinator.com", "b@gmail.com", "c@fake.notarealtld"] }
```

```json
{
  "results": [
    { "email": "a@mailinator.com", "domain": "mailinator.com", "valid_tld": true, "has_mx": true, "dns_blocked": false, "disposable": true, "should_reject": true },
    { "email": "b@gmail.com", "domain": "gmail.com", "valid_tld": true, "has_mx": true, "dns_blocked": false, "disposable": false, "should_reject": false },
    { "email": "c@fake.notarealtld", "domain": "fake.notarealtld", "valid_tld": false, "has_mx": false, "disposable": false, "should_reject": true }
  ]
}
```

### Batch check domains

```
POST /check
Content-Type: application/json

{ "domains": ["mailinator.com", "yahoo.com"] }
```

```json
{
  "results": [
    { "domain": "mailinator.com", "valid_tld": true, "has_mx": true, "dns_blocked": false, "disposable": true, "should_reject": true },
    { "domain": "yahoo.com", "valid_tld": true, "has_mx": true, "dns_blocked": false, "disposable": false, "should_reject": false }
  ]
}
```

### Filter stats

```
GET /stats
```

```json
{
  "itemCount": 139000,
  "bitCount": 2000000,
  "hashCount": 10,
  "byteSize": 250000,
  "falsePositiveRate": 0.004
}
```

## Response fields

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `valid_tld` | boolean | `true` if the domain ends in a real ICANN-recognized TLD (`.com`, `.co.uk`, etc). `false` means the address can't possibly receive mail. |
| `has_mx` | boolean | `true` if the domain has MX records (can receive email). `false` means the domain doesn't exist or has no mail server. |
| `dns_blocked` | boolean | `true` if Cloudflare family DNS appeared to block an otherwise email-capable domain. Omitted when `has_mx` is `false` because filtered-DNS checks are skipped. |
| `dns_blocked_category` | string | Optional when `dns_blocked` is `true`: `malware`, `family`, or `unknown`, inferred by comparing Cloudflare family DNS with malware-only DNS. |
| `disposable` | boolean | `true` if the domain is in the disposable-email blocklist. Only meaningful when `valid_tld` is `true`. |
| `should_reject` | boolean | `true` when the rules below say to reject (invalid TLD, no MX, disposable, or filtered-DNS blocked). |

## How to interpret results

Use **`should_reject`** for a single accept/reject gate, or read the fields individually:

1. **`valid_tld: false`** -> reject. The domain is not real.
2. **`has_mx: false`** -> reject. The domain has no mail server and can't receive email.
3. **`valid_tld: true`, `has_mx: true`, `disposable: true`** -> reject. Known throwaway provider.
4. **`valid_tld: true`, `has_mx: true`, `dns_blocked: true`** -> reject. Blocked by filtered DNS.
5. **`valid_tld: true`, `has_mx: true`, `disposable: false`, `dns_blocked: false`** -> accept.

No API key needed. No rate limits currently enforced.

Built by the people at [SSLBoard](https://sslboard.com).

## Agent discovery

- `GET /llms-full.txt` - expanded machine-readable documentation with discovery links.
- `GET /auth.md` - explicit no-auth policy. No API key, OAuth, protected resources, or commerce flow exists.
- `GET /openapi.json` - OpenAPI 3.1 contract for the REST API.
- `GET /api-catalog.json` - API catalog metadata.
- `GET /.well-known/mcp-server.json` - MCP server card for validation tools.
- `GET /.well-known/webmcp` - WebMCP-compatible discovery metadata.
- `GET /mcp` - lightweight JSON-RPC endpoint supporting `tools/list` and `tools/call` for `check_email`, `check_domain`, `batch_check_emails`, `batch_check_domains`, and `get_stats`.
- `GET /.well-known/agent-skills.json` - agent usage guidance.
- `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` - stateless validation agent card.

The homepage supports `Accept: text/markdown` and `?format=markdown` for text-first clients.

## Limits and safety

No API key is required. Request bodies are capped at 100000 bytes and batch requests are capped at 1000 emails or domains. Disposable email detection is an abuse-prevention signal, not proof of malicious intent.
